title: Microsoft Intune: Windows quality update policies with per-type approval (GCC)
summary: Hold: the release-control path ends at Approve even though it also promises to pause updates. The custom-role instructions omit required device-access permissions, automatic enrolment omits the Windows Insider exception, and the licensing model should describe an included entitlement rather than mixed licensing.

claims.quote: Manage individual Windows quality updates including non-Security and out of band updates.  Choose which update types to automatically approve and the rollout options for those approvals.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Each update type can use automatic or manual approval, with different methods in one policy.
claims.quote: A single policy can use both automatic and manual methods across different update types.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Automatic approval offers updates after a configured deferral of 0 to 30 days.
claims.quote: Devices assigned to this policy receive an update after this many days since Microsoft releases the update. Adjust each ring’s deferral as needed. The allowed range is 0 to 30 days for quality updates.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Monthly security updates default to automatic approval when a policy is created.
claims.quote: When you create a quality update policy, the default approval configuration of monthly security updates is automatic.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The other three update types default to manual approval in a new policy.
claims.quote: The default approval configuration of other updates is manual.

claims.claim: The policy settings also govern supported .NET Framework updates.
claims.quote: The quality update policy settings also govern supported .NET Framework updates in Windows Autopatch.

claims.claim: Manual approval holds deployment until explicit approval, making unowned approvals a patch-delay risk.
claims.quote: This configuration provides full control, deploying updates only with explicit manual approval.

claims.claim: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic security approvals and manual optional-update approvals.
claims.quote: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approvals for security updates and manual approvals for optional updates.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: devices without a quality update policy continue their standard Windows Update behaviour.
claims.quote: Devices without a quality update policy continue to receive quality updates through standard Windows Update behavior, using update rings and Windows Update client policies to control deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications.

claims.claim: Approval settings are reached in Microsoft Intune admin center through Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Create > Windows quality update policy > Settings.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates. Select Create. Select Windows quality update policy. Under Settings, choose your approval method configuration for security updates, non-security updates, and out-of-band updates.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies creates a policy with its approval and deferral settings.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies
"approvalSettings": [{ "approvalMethodType": "automatic", "deferredDeploymentInDay": 7 }]

claims.claim: The approvalSettings collection carries approvalMethodType and deferredDeploymentInDay.
claims.quote: "approvalSettings": [{ "@odata.type": "microsoft.graph.windowsQualityUpdateApprovalSetting", "windowsQualityUpdateCadence": "String", "windowsQualityUpdateCategory": "String", "approvalMethodType": "String", "deferredDeploymentInDay": 1024 }]

claims.claim: hotpatchEnabled controls whether hotpatch is enabled.
claims.quote: hotpatchEnabled | Boolean | Indicates if hotpatch is enabled for the tenants. When 'true', tenant can apply quality updates without rebooting their devices. When 'false', tenant devices will receive cold patch associated with Windows quality updates.

claims.claim: The path ending in Approved policies > policy > Approve governs both approving and pausing an individual release.
claims.quote: To pause a cloud-based quality update deployment: Select the X of Y under Approved policies to see which policies are approved. Select the desired policies and select Pause.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].governs and the rendered row label to 'Approving an individual quality update release for a policy'. Keep the approval path. Add to its note: 'To pause a release in the UI, follow the same route and select Pause instead of Approve.' The cited overview documents both actions.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction can approve or pause quality updates.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction
 action | windowsQualityUpdatePolicyActionType
 ids | String collection
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/intune-softwareupdate-windowsqualityupdatepolicyactiontype?view=graph-rest-beta to sources. Replace the API portion of controls[1].note with 'Beta endpoint. The request body takes action and ids; action=approve approves a quality update and action=suspend pauses it.' The linked enum reference explicitly documents both meanings.

claims.claim: The bulkAction page takes action and ids, exemplifies suspend, and does not itself describe the other action values.
claims.quote:
action | windowsQualityUpdatePolicyActionType | 
ids | String collection | 
"action": "suspend"

claims.claim: Pausing an approved update revokes its approval.
claims.quote: When paused, Windows Autopatch revokes the approval of the update

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: No new devices receive a paused release.
claims.quote: When paused, Windows Autopatch revokes the approval of the update, and no new devices receive it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Pausing does not roll back devices that already installed the update.
claims.quote: Devices that already installed the update aren't rolled back.

claims.quote: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new update pause settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Quality update policies take priority over update rings for approval settings and deferrals on devices with both.
claims.quote: Device assigned to Windows Update ring policies and cloud-based quality update policies. The quality update policy takes priority for approval settings and deferrals.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Other update ring client settings, including deadlines and grace periods, remain active.
claims.quote: Other update ring policy settings, such as deadlines and grace periods, remain active.

claims.claim: With both cloud-based and legacy hotpatch-only quality policies, monthly security updates are not offered until approved manually or automatically.
claims.quote: Device assigned to cloud-based quality update policy and legacy quality update policy (with only the hotpatch update setting). The cloud-based quality update policy takes priority. That is, monthly security updates aren't offered to the device until you either manually or automatically approve them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Changing an existing policy's approval method requires creating a new policy.
claims.quote: No, you can't change the approval method in an existing policy. If you need a different approval method, create a new policy.

claims.claim: An administrator can manually approve an update before an automatic deferral ends.
claims.quote: If a policy is set to automatic approval with a deferral period, can I manually override the deferral and approve the update immediately? Yes, you can manually override the deferral period and approve the update when needed.

claims.claim: Learn recommends keeping quality update deferrals under three days.
claims.quote: Keep quality update deferrals under three days.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Approving non-security updates does not deliver them to hotpatch-enabled devices; disable the policy's hotpatch setting to receive them.
claims.quote: No, the devices won't receive non-security updates in this case. ... To receive non-security updates, disable the hotpatch update setting in the quality update policy.

claims.claim: Windows Enterprise LTSC is unsupported for this policy type and Learn directs administrators to update rings instead.
claims.quote: Windows Enterprise LTSC (Long Term Service Channel) isn't supported. Use update ring policies instead.
claims.fix: Replace the LTSC statement with 'The Intune Manage Windows quality updates page says Windows Enterprise LTSC is unsupported for this policy type and directs administrators to update rings; the cited Windows Autopatch overview and prerequisites pages separately say Autopatch supports quality-update management for currently serviced Windows 10/11 LTSC devices.' This reports the disagreement without changing the documented Intune restriction.

claims.claim: Windows 10 ESU devices receive .NET Framework updates according to client settings, so policy approvals apply only to OS quality updates on those devices.
claims.quote: Windows 10 devices enrolled in Extended Security Updates (ESU) continue to receive .NET Framework updates from Windows Update based on client-side settings. Therefore, quality update policy approval settings apply only to OS quality updates on those devices.
